title: Philippines Archaeological Record Deep Composition Analysis

cave_rock_shelter.notes: Tabon complex 218 caves (38 with archaeology), Penablanca 100+, Mindoro 40+

open_air.notes: Cagayan Valley 168+ open-air, Rizal-Bulacan 120, Calatagan hundreds, Batanes

burial_non_cave.notes: Most are Protohistoric (Calatagan, Santa Ana, Boljoon)

pre_400CE_breakdown.key_insight: Philippines pre-400 CE record is NOT predominantly cave-based. Open-air sites are the majority.

key_volcanoes_with_nearby_archaeology: Iraya (Sunget, Anaro, Naidi — Neolithic sites under ash)

hypothesis_test.H0: Philippines archaeology predominantly cave-based (weakens Java argument)
hypothesis_test.H1: Philippines has diverse record including open-air (strengthens Java argument)
hypothesis_test.key_evidence: Open-air sites = 50% of all documented sites, 55-65% of pre-400 CE sites

strengths_of_taphonomic_argument: Open-air sites genuinely abundant in Philippines (not cave-dominated)
Philippine volcanic zones retain 25-40 pre-400 CE sites
All material culture categories present in Philippines, absent in volcanic Java
Pinatubo proves volcanic burial preserves sites (if excavated)
Iraya ash buried and preserved Neolithic sites in Batanes
Batangas/Taal comparison devastating (39+ eruptions, rich archaeology nearby)
weaknesses_of_taphonomic_argument: Oldest sites (>10,000 BP) are mostly cave-based
4,000+ total sites figure may be inflated (500-1,000 well-documented)
Open-air sites concentrated in well-surveyed regions (Cagayan, Batangas)
Some Philippine volcanic zones have sparse records too
Philippines island geography creates coastal proximity advantage
Poor organic preservation is shared problem (not differentiator)
